positions.title: Graduate Research Assistant, Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering and Medical Imaging
positions.description:
Performed a feasibility study for achieving real-time image segmentation (using both CPU & GPU
implementations) for hippocampal and thalamic regions in the brain.

Implemented and validated a novel real-time multi-atlas segmentation approach for thalamic
nuclei in the brain using 3-D magnetic resonance images. Validation was performed using
statistical data analysis.

Designed, implemented and validated an automated image registration-segmentation-rendering
procedure for direct visual targeting of a specific thalamic nucleus (VLP) for neurosurgery.

positions.title: Graduate Teaching Assistant, Department of Physics
positions.description: Was responsible for conducting weekly laboratory sessions for Introductory Mechanics as well as grading of lab sessions, home-works and exams.

positions.title: Teaching Assistant
positions.description: Taught basics of aeronautics and handled summer camps for grades 4-9 in alternating sessions on a weekly basis for six weeks at the Wildcats Aeronautics Camp. The camp’s framework was designed in collaboration with NASA.

positions.title: Graduate Teaching Assistant, Department of Atmospheric Sciences
positions.description: Graded home-works and essays and provided individual feedback to students in improving their writing skills for their essays.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Worked on embedded programming of control systems including integration of new features for next generation thermostats. Development was primarily in C & C++ in combination with shell scripting in a Linux environment. Perforce was used for code revision with Eclipse as the primary IDE.

Performed black box testing of the software updates before release from the development team. Testing was performed directly on the thermostats using an in-house testing kit designed to simulate the actual inter-connected mechanical equipment.

positions.title: Summer Intern
positions.description: Implemented a new model based on patch-wise representation and dictionary update of frames and, excellent results were obtained with absolute foreground reproduction and complete adaptability to abrupt changes in luminosity. This was accomplished in Matlab after initial trials in OpenCV.

projects.title: Mammogram Classification Using A Novel Segmentation Technique
projects.description:
• Proposed and implemented a two stage segmentation technique with a pre-segmentation stage preceding it.

• Feature Extraction and Classification performed using two feature sets and four different classifiers (BPN, RBF, LVQ, and SVM).

• Excellent results (in terms of accuracy) were obtained when the SVM classifier was combined with the improved segmentation as compared to other classifiers, with the execution time low enough for real time usage.

projects.title: Background Subtraction  using Sparse Representation
projects.description:
• Implemented the previously existing models.

• Proposed and implemented a new model based on Patch-wise Representation and Dictionary Update.

• Excellent results were obtained with absolute foreground reproduction and complete adaptability to sudden changes in luminosity.
